newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger on favorable U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger on favorable U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Friday, as U.S. economic reports suggesting inflation is not accelerating helped strengthen markets in both countries, analysts said.

"The last remaining hurdle this week was the (U.S.) GDP report. I think a lot of people were encouraged by the fact that the implicit price deflator rose by only 1.4 percent," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed income research at ABN AMRO Bank Canada. Canada's 30-year bond rose C$1.20 to C$109.15 to yield 7.217 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 28/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
A report that Canada's real gross domestic product rose 0.5 percent in November, compared with expectations of a 0.4 percent rise, had little market impact, dealers said.

Analysts said Canadian bond investors will remain focused on the United States next week. In addition to the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee on Tuesday and Wednesday, investors are also awaiting key U.S. payrolls data for January on Friday.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.80 to C$103.25 to yield 6.543 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 17/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
The spread between the Canadian and U.S. benchmark bonds was three basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.86 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.15 percent.
